summary.text: Stellar classification sorts stars by the features in their spectrum, the rainbow you get when a prism or grating splits a star's light.
Lines in that rainbow each point to an element or molecule, and their strengths vary mainly with the temperature of the star's photosphere.
Most stars get a letter from O (hottest) to M (coolest), then a digit from 0 (hottest) to 9 (coolest).

facts.label: Letter order
facts.value: O, B, A, F, G, K, M, from hottest to coolest

facts.label: The Sun's class
facts.value: G2V, with a surface around 5,800 K

facts.label: Digit meaning
facts.value: 0 is the hottest in a class, 9 the coolest

facts.label: Who showed temperature
facts.value: Cecilia Payne showed the letter sequence is a temperature sequence

items.prompt: Two stars are both in class A. One is labelled A1 and the other A8. Which statement is right?

options.label: A8 is the hotter star, because 8 is larger
Both have the same temperature within a class
A1 is the hotter star, because 0 is hottest
Neither label says anything about temperature

items.explain: Within a class the digit runs from 0 (hottest) to 9 (coolest), so A1 is hotter than A8.

items.prompt: Each line in a star's spectrum points to one chemical element. What does a line's strength indicate?

options.label: How much of that element is present
How old the star is
How fast the star is spinning
How far away the star is

items.explain: Each line marks an element or molecule, and the strength of the line shows how abundant it is.

items.prompt: A star's full label is G2V. What does the V at the end tell you?

options.label: It is a bright giant
It is a white dwarf
It is a hypergiant
It is a main-sequence star

items.explain: The Roman numeral is the luminosity class, and class V is used for main-sequence stars, as in the Sun's G2V.

items.prompt: Early astronomers lined up stars as O, B, A, F, G, K, M without knowing why the order worked. What did later work show it to be?

options.label: A ranking by how far away the stars are
A sequence of temperature
A ranking by how old the stars are
A sequence of star size

items.explain: The sequence predates the understanding that it tracks temperature; Cecilia Payne showed that it does.

items.prompt: A book calls one star 'red' and another 'blue', yet to the eye stars look paler than those words suggest. Why?

options.label: Stars give off every colour, and combined colours look white
Earth's air washes out every star's colour
Stars only give off white light
The eye cannot see the peak colour of a star

items.explain: Colour names only count the peak of the spectrum, but stars radiate in all parts of it, and all colours together look white.

items.prompt: Two stars share the same temperature, but one is a giant and the other a dwarf. What in their spectra helps tell them apart?

options.label: The giant always has the earlier letter
The giant always has a higher digit
The giant has more spectral lines in total
The width of certain absorption lines

items.explain: The width of some absorption lines depends on the density of the star's atmosphere, which separates giants from dwarfs.
